chromeos-base/crosvm: drop crosvm-usb USE flag This flag is misleadingly named: it sounds like it should control whether USB support is enabled, but in fact it actually just controlled the 'sandboxed-libusb' feature flag, and USB support is always enabled regardless of the USE flag state. The USE flag also (incorrectly) controlled whether the dependency on libusb was added; building without USE=crosvm-usb would still link against libusb but without declaring the dependency in the portage dep graph. Building without sandboxed-libusb enabled won't work at all in the Chrome OS environment, since we need to be able to pass USB devices via file descriptor, which is only accepted when crosvm is built with sandboxed-libusb. This is reinforced by the fact that crosvm-usb is enabled by default in the ebuild (via +) and is never disabled in any existing board profiles. To avoid confusion and clean up the ebuild, drop the crosvm-usb flag entirely, and always build with the sandboxed-libsub feature enabled.
